info.title: Tackle Co-Sell for Google Cloud Channel Customer Engagements
info.description:
This API helps you interact with Google Cloud Channel to create and manage
co-sell opportunities that you share with Google as well as receive, respond
to, and manage opportunities originated by Google.

Request and response shapes mirror Google Cloud Channel's v1alpha1
opportunity model. Every opportunity payload also carries a
`$tkl-metadata` block with Tackle-specific extensions for CRM linkage,
Salesforce sync status, and attribute-syncing subscription state.

## Authentication

This API requires a Tackle machine-to-machine (M2M) access token. Issue
your M2M client credentials following the [How to get an M2M client ID
and secret](https://developers.tackle.io/docs/how-to-get-an-m2m-client-id-and-secret)
guide, exchange them for an access token following the [Getting an
access token](https://developers.tackle.io/docs/getting-an-access-token)
guide, then send the token with each request in the `Authorization`
header as `Bearer <access_token>`.

The token supplies the vendor and organization context for every request
and authorizes specific actions via permission scopes. Each operation
below documents the permission scope it requires; a request made by a
credential that does not hold the required scope is rejected with
`403 Forbidden`. When provisioning M2M credentials, include the scopes
that match the operations your integration intends to call.

## Related Tackle Co-Sell APIs

Tackle publishes equivalent Co-Sell APIs for other cloud providers. The
APIs are not interchangeable: AWS and Google Cloud Channel use
"opportunities," Microsoft Partner Center uses "referrals," and each
provider has its own paths, payload shapes, and pagination conventions.

- Tackle Co-Sell for AWS: https://aws.cosell.tackle.io
- Tackle Co-Sell for Microsoft Partner Center: https://msft.cosell.tackle.io

tags.name: Opportunities
tags.description:
Create, read, update, and audit co-sell opportunities shared
with Google Cloud Channel.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description:
Vendor-level reference data, including the picklist endpoint
that supplies the acceptable values for opportunity fields.

get.description:
Returns a page of opportunities for the authenticated vendor.
Supports free-text search, multiple term filters, a `cloudCreated`
date range, and sorting.

Requires the `cosell:ListOpportunities` permission.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Free-text search across `title`, `companyName`, `cloudProviderID`,
and `crmID` with "and"-style bool prefix matching.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
Zero-based index of the first result in the page. The
server validates that the value parses as an integer, so always pass an
integer >= 0.

parameters.name: pagesize
parameters.description:
Maximum number of results in the page. Note: the canonical
wire form is the all-lowercase `pagesize` (intentional). For
compatibility, the server also accepts `pageSize`.

parameters.name: sortField
parameters.description:
Field to sort on. Each value names a sort key as exposed by
this endpoint and corresponds to a field (or pair of fields)
on the `Opportunity` payload:

- `cloudProviderID` — the Google Cloud Channel opportunity
  identifier (the trailing ID portion of `name`).
- `cloudStatus` — the `state` field.
- `cloudSalesStage` — the `stage` field.
- `cloudCreated` — the `createTime` field.
- `cloudLastModified` — the `updateTime` field.
- `targetCloseDate` — the qualified target close date for
  the opportunity.
- `rebateExpirationDate` — `partnerInfo.rebateExpirationDate`.

parameters.name: crmID
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more CRM IDs (repeat the query parameter for
multiple values).

parameters.name: cloudStatus
parameters.description:
Filter by the opportunity's `state` field. Repeatable.
Values are the same `State` enum returned on the response.

parameters.name: cloudSalesStage
parameters.description:
Filter by the opportunity's `stage` field. Repeatable.
Values are the same `Stage` enum returned on the response.

parameters.name: operationType
parameters.description: Filter by transaction operation type. Repeatable.

parameters.name: hasErrors
parameters.description:
When `true` returns only opportunities that currently have a
cloud error count; when `false`, only those without.

parameters.name: hasSalesforceErrors
parameters.description:
When `true` returns only opportunities that have a Salesforce
error count; when `false`, only those without.

parameters.name: hasCrmID
parameters.description:
When `true` returns only opportunities that are linked to a CRM
record; when `false`, only those that are not.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) on the opportunity's `createTime`
(the `cloudCreated` sort key), formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) on the opportunity's `createTime`
(the `cloudCreated` sort key), formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

post.description:
Creates an opportunity in Tackle and asynchronously dispatches a
Google Cloud Channel `opportunities.create` request. The response
contains the newly minted Tackle-side `id` and the `requestId` of
the dispatched cloud operation; poll
`GET /api/opportunities/{id}` or
`GET /api/opportunities/{id}/events` to observe the cloud outcome.

The `tackle-operation-id` header selects the sub-operation:

- `createOpportunity` (default): the `state` value in the
  request body is honored as-is. Requires
  `cosell:CreateOpportunity`. If the body's `state` is
  `SUBMITTED`, `cosell:StartEngagement` is additionally
  required.
- `createDraftOpportunity`: the body's `state` must be
  `DRAFT`; any other value produces a `400`. Requires
  `cosell:CreateOpportunity`.

`qualificationInfo.legalLanguageAccepted` must be `true`.

parameters.name: tackle-operation-id
parameters.description:
Selects the create sub-operation. Defaults to
`createOpportunity` when omitted. Any other value (including
update-side operations such as `updateOpportunity` or
`submitOpportunity`) is rejected with a `400 Bad Request`.

202.description: Opportunity recorded in Tackle and cloud create request enqueued.

get.description:
Returns the full Tackle-shaped opportunity including
`$tkl-metadata` and the latest cached Cloud Channel payload.

Requires the `cosell:GetOpportunity` permission.

post.description:
Queues a partial update against the Cloud Channel API. The exact
behavior depends on `tackle-operation-id`:

- `updateOpportunity` (default): requires `cosell:UpdateOpportunity`.
  If the resulting state transitions the opportunity to `SUBMITTED`
  (from anything other than `SUBMITTED`), `cosell:StartEngagement`
  is additionally required and the effective operation is treated
  as `submitOpportunity`.
- `updateDraftOpportunity`: requires
  `cosell:UpdateOpportunity`.
- `submitOpportunity`: forces `state` to `SUBMITTED`; requires
  `cosell:StartEngagement`.
- `closeWonOpportunity` / `closeLostOpportunity`: request a close;
  requires `cosell:UpdateOpportunity`.
- `retryCreateOpportunity`: requeue a create that previously
  failed; requires `cosell:UpdateOpportunity` and
  `legalLanguageAccepted: true`.
- Test-environment-only:
  `acceptOpportunity`, `rejectOpportunity`,
  `closeByAdminOpportunity`, `confirmCloseWonOpportunity`,
  `confirmCloseLostOpportunity`. These simulate Google-side actions
  and attribute the resulting history event to Google.

The response returns a `requestId` identifying the enqueued cloud
operation; poll `GET /api/opportunities/{id}/events` or
`GET /api/opportunities/{id}` to observe the outcome.

get.summary: List the event history for an opportunity
get.description:
Returns a page of history events for an opportunity. Each event
has an `operation` field identifying what produced it; the
documented operations include the values an integrator can
submit on the `tackle-operation-id` header, plus two
service-emitted operations (`internalUpdateEvent`,
`cloudUpdateEvent`) — see `HistoryOperationId` for the full
catalog. Treat the field as a free-form string and fall back to
a default branch when displaying an unknown value.

Unknown opportunity IDs return `200` with an empty `events`
array — this endpoint does not distinguish "no events" from
"no such opportunity." This behavior is asymmetric with
`GET /api/opportunities/{id}`, which returns `404` for unknown
IDs.

Requires the `cosell:ListOpportunityEvents` permission.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Maximum number of events to return. Values above 25 are
silently clamped to 25. When omitted (or `0`), the server does
not apply a per-page item limit; the page is bounded only by an internal response size limit and may include many
more than 25 events. Pass an explicit `limit` for predictable
page sizes and use the returned `next` token to paginate.

parameters.name: next
parameters.description:
Opaque continuation token returned by a previous call.
Pass it back unmodified to fetch the next page. The token
is opaque; do not rely on its internal format (malformed
tokens surface as `500 Internal Server Error` rather than
`400 Bad Request`, so always pass back the token from a
prior response unmodified).

200.description:
A page of events. Returned with an empty `events` array
when the supplied opportunity ID does not exist for the
authenticated vendor.

get.summary: Get picklist options for Opportunity fields
get.description:
Returns the acceptable values for enumerable `Opportunity`
fields, plus reference lists for country, language, and
currency codes. Use this endpoint to populate picklist UI
controls so that the values an integrator surfaces stay in
step with the values the API accepts (which can be a subset
of the corresponding schema enum — see the `PicklistOptions`
schema for details).

The response is an object keyed by field path
(for example `.customerInfo.customerDetails.address.regionCode`);
each value is the array of acceptable
`{ display, value }` options for that field.

The response also contains a `.dataMapper.stage` key. This key
is a curated subset of the `Stage` enum used by Tackle's Data
Mapper feature when importing opportunity data from external
systems. It does not correspond to any field on the
`Opportunity` payload, and most integrators using this API
directly can ignore it.

Requires the `cosell:GetPicklistOptions` permission.

200.description: Picklist options keyed by field path.

bearerAuth.description: Tackle machine-to-machine access token sent as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

TackleOperationIdHeader.name: tackle-operation-id
TackleOperationIdHeader.description:
Narrows the effective operation on `POST /api/opportunities/{id}`.
See the operation description for the accepted values and the
permissions required for each. Create-only values
(`createOpportunity`, `createDraftOpportunity`) are rejected with
a `400 Bad Request` because creates must be sent to
`POST /api/opportunities` instead.

BadRequest.description:
The request was malformed or failed validation. Common triggers
include missing required fields, invalid enum values, type
mismatches, an unrecognized `tackle-operation-id`, and (for
create) `qualificationInfo.legalLanguageAccepted` not being
`true`. The response `message` describes the specific
violation.

Forbidden.description: The caller is not authorized to perform this action.

NotFound.description: The requested resource does not exist.

Conflict.description:
The request conflicts with existing state. For
`createOpportunity` and `updateOpportunity`, this is returned
when the supplied `$tkl-metadata.crm.id` is already linked to
another co-sell opportunity for the same vendor.

Locked.description:
The vendor's co-sell configuration is in the middle of a reset
and cannot accept changes. Retry the request after a short
delay; if the lock persists for more than a few minutes,
contact Tackle support.

InternalServerError.description:
An unexpected error occurred while processing the request.
Retry idempotent reads after a short delay; for writes, check
the opportunity history (`GET /api/opportunities/{id}/events`)
before retrying to confirm whether the prior request was
applied.

Error.description:
Error response body. The service emits only a human-readable
`message`. A request identifier may be included in response headers for support and troubleshooting.

Opportunity.description:
Tackle's opportunity payload. Mirrors the Google Cloud Channel
`Opportunity` (v1alpha1) schema and adds a `$tkl-metadata`
block carrying Tackle-specific state — CRM linkage,
attribute-syncing subscription ID, and Salesforce sync error
summary.

name.description:
Resource name of the opportunity in the form
`opportunities/{opportunity_id}`. Populated by Google Cloud
Channel after the first successful create; integrators
should treat this field as read-only — values supplied on
create or update are ignored.

customerDisplayName.description:
Output only. Display name for the customer organization as
resolved by Google Cloud Channel. May be normalized or
disambiguated relative to the
`customerInfo.customerDetails.organizationName` value
submitted on create.

stateDescription.description: Output only. Reason the opportunity was not accepted.

owner.description:
Output only. Name of the Google field sales representative
(FSR) who owns the opportunity inside Google.

ownerEmail.description:
Output only. Email of the Google field sales representative
(FSR) who owns the opportunity inside Google.

creatorEmail.description:
Output only. Email associated with the creator of the
opportunity. For opportunities created via this API, this
is the email associated with the integrator's M2M client
credentials (see the Authentication section in the spec
description). For opportunities created elsewhere (such as
the Tackle UI), this is the human user's email.

opportunityLines.description: Output only. Populated after the opportunity is accepted.

opportunityTeamMembers.description: Output only. Populated after the opportunity is accepted.

customerContacts.description: Output only. Populated after the opportunity is accepted.

createTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the opportunity was created.

updateTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the opportunity was last updated.

referenceOpportunityId.description:
Output only. Opportunity ID in Google's legacy Partner
Advantage Portal. Useful for integrators reconciling Cloud
Channel opportunities with records that originated in
Partner Advantage; can be ignored by integrators that work
only with Cloud Channel.

submitterEmail.description:
Optional. User email that created the opportunity through an
integrator. Only used for integrator-created opportunities. Can
only be set on create and cannot be edited thereafter.

OpportunityMetadata.description:
Tackle-specific metadata attached to every opportunity. Carried in
the `$tkl-metadata` key of the payload.

companyName.description:
Convenience copy of the customer organization name,
populated for list views and search. Updated whenever the
underlying customer record changes; integrators that need
the canonical name should read
`customerInfo.customerDetails.organizationName`.

pendingRequestIds.description:
Request IDs for in-flight operations that have been queued
but not yet applied to the cloud. Empty array when no
requests are pending.

cloudError.description:
The last cloud error encountered, cleared on the next
successful request. Absent when no error has been recorded.

hasCloudErrors.description:
True when the opportunity has unresolved cloud-side errors —
that is, the most recent cloud operation failed and no
subsequent successful operation has cleared the error.

archivedAt.description:
Timestamp when the opportunity was archived in Tackle; absent
otherwise.

hasSalesforceErrors.description:
True when the opportunity has unresolved Salesforce-sync
errors — that is, the most recent sync attempt failed and
no subsequent successful sync has cleared the error.

salesforceSyncError.description:
The last Salesforce sync error, if any. Absent when no
error has been recorded.

dataMapperToken.description:
Write-only. Token issued by Tackle's Data Mapper feature
(the Tackle product that imports opportunity data from
external systems and keeps selected fields in sync over
time). When provided on create, the new opportunity is
subscribed to ongoing attribute syncing from the source
data set the token references. Integrators not using Data
Mapper can omit this field.

created.description: Timestamp when the opportunity was created in Tackle.

lastModified.description: Timestamp when the opportunity was last modified in Tackle.

OpportunityCRMInfo.description:
CRM linkage for the opportunity. Both fields are nullable so that
callers can explicitly clear them.

OpportunityAttributeSyncing.description:
Subscription information for opportunities whose attributes are
kept in sync with an upstream data source through Tackle's Data
Mapper feature. Present only when attribute syncing is enabled
for this opportunity; omitted otherwise.

subscriptionId.description:
Attribute-syncing subscription ID. Pass this value back to
Data Mapper to unsubscribe the opportunity from its current
data source — for example, when the opportunity is being
re-linked to a different CRM record.

CreateOpportunityRequest.description:
Tackle-shaped opportunity payload for create.

The API validates up front that `opportunityInfo` and
`qualificationInfo` are present and that
`qualificationInfo.legalLanguageAccepted` is `true`; any of
these missing or `false` produces a `400`. The remaining
Google-Cloud-Channel-required fields (notably `customerInfo`
and its nested `customerDetails.organizationName`, `domain`,
`address.regionCode`, and `employeeCount`) are not checked
up front — the request is dispatched to Google Cloud Channel,
and any downstream validation failure surfaces as an event
on the opportunity history. Poll
`GET /api/opportunities/{id}/events` to observe that outcome.

The API forces `opportunityInfo.partnerEntity` to the calling
vendor's configured partner ID and `source` to `PARTNER`;
values supplied for those two fields in the request are
ignored.

requestId.description:
Identifier for the enqueued cloud operation. Matches the
`eventID` reported on subsequent history events.

UpdateOpportunityRequest.description:
Tackle-shaped opportunity payload for update. Only the fields the
caller wants to change need to be present; the server merges with
the existing opportunity. The opportunity `name` is immutable and
is always overridden by the server with the stored value.

requestId.description:
Identifier for the enqueued cloud operation. Matches the
`eventID` reported on subsequent history events.

total.description: Total number of opportunities matching the query.

currentPageCount.description: Number of items in this page.

nextIndex.description:
Offset to pass as `from` to retrieve the next page. Omitted
when there is no next page.

isNextPage.description: True when more results are available after this page.

next.description:
Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omitted when the
page is the last.

operation.description:
The operation that produced this history event. See
`HistoryOperationId` for the common set of values, but
treat this field as a free-form string: additional
operation strings beyond the documented catalog may
appear. Clients should fall back to a default branch
when displaying an unknown value.

eventID.description:
Unique identifier for the history event. Equal in value to
the `requestId` returned by the create or update response
that produced the event; the two schema families use
different casing on the wire (`eventID` here, `requestId`
on the response body) but carry the same identifier.

status.description:
Status of the event. Omitted from the response body for
instantaneous history items that have no async lifecycle.

rawRequest.description: The original Tackle-shaped request that produced this event.

cloudRaw.description: Raw cloud payload, if any, associated with this event.

created.description: Timestamp the event was created (RFC 3339 Nano).

lastModified.description: Timestamp the event was last updated (RFC 3339 Nano).

OpportunityHistoryEventActivityDetails.description:
Human-readable details about a history event, intended for
display in opportunity audit trails.

OpportunityHistoryEventPrincipal.description:
Actor attribution for a history event. For test-environment-only
operations (`acceptOpportunity`, `rejectOpportunity`,
`closeByAdminOpportunity`, `confirmCloseWonOpportunity`,
`confirmCloseLostOpportunity`) the principal is set to a
Google placeholder so that the resulting event renders as
Google-attributed in opportunity audit trails.

id.description:
Stable identifier for the principal (for example, a Tackle
user ID, integrator service-account ID, or Google sales
user ID).

type.description:
Principal kind. Common values include `user`, `integrator`,
`cloud`, and `internal`. Treat as a free-form string and
fall back to a default branch when displaying an unknown
value.

givenName.description:
Given (first) name of the principal, when known. May be
absent for non-human principals.

familyName.description:
Family (last) name of the principal, when known. May be
absent for non-human principals.

pictureUrl.description: Optional URL of the principal's avatar image.

email.description: Email of the principal, when known.

OpportunityHistoryEventCloudRequest.description:
One Google Cloud Channel call made on behalf of an opportunity
history event. A single event may include multiple cloud
requests (for example, when a sub-flow chains calls).

requestID.description:
Identifier for the cloud-side request, useful for support
correlation. Equal to the `eventID` of the parent history
event for top-level requests.

timestamp.description: Time the cloud request was issued.

request.description:
The raw request payload sent to Google Cloud Channel.
Shape mirrors the cloud's v1alpha1 schema.

OpportunityHistoryEventCloudResponse.description:
The Google Cloud Channel response received for a corresponding
`OpportunityHistoryEventCloudRequest`.

requestID.description:
Cloud-side request identifier this response corresponds to.
Matches the `requestID` of the paired
`OpportunityHistoryEventCloudRequest`.

operation.description: Cloud Channel operation name that was invoked.

timestamp.description: Time the cloud response was received.

response.description:
The raw response payload received from Google Cloud Channel.
Shape mirrors the cloud's v1alpha1 schema.

error.description:
Cloud-side error message when the response represents a
failure. Omitted on success.

PicklistOptions.description:
Object keyed by field path; each value is the array of acceptable
picklist options for that field. Additional field paths may be
added over time as the `Opportunity` schema evolves.

Most keys correspond to a field on the `Opportunity` schema and
mirror the values currently offered for that field. The picklist
is treated as the source of truth for what to surface in
integrator UIs: an enum value that appears in this API's schema
but is no longer offered by Google may be omitted from the
picklist, so the picklist values for a given field can be a
subset of the corresponding enum.

Country, language, and currency codes are populated from public
standards: `.customerInfo.customerDetails.address.regionCode`
returns ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region codes,
`.customerInfo.customerDetails.address.languageCode` returns
BCP-47 language codes, and
`.qualificationInfo.dealSize.currencyCode` returns ISO 4217
currency codes.

The `.dataMapper.stage` key is an exception: it is a curated
subset of the `Stage` enum used by Tackle's Data Mapper feature
when importing opportunity data from external systems. It does
not correspond to any field on the `Opportunity` payload;
integrators not using Data Mapper can ignore it.

value.description: The value to send in the request payload.

default.description:
`true` when this option is the default for the field. Only
one option per field is marked as default; absent if no
default is defined.

partnerEntity.description:
Required. Partner who sources the deal. For 2-tier partners
this is the distributor ID. Format: `partners/{id}`.

indirectPartnerEntity.description:
Optional. For 2-tier deals, the indirect reseller. Format:
`partners/{id}`.

displayName.description: Optional. Display name for the opportunity.

productFamily.description: Product Family. Required for ISV Solution Connect Opportunity.

productCategory.description: Product Category. Required for non-ISV opportunities.

confidential.description:
Optional. Flag to identify if the opportunity is confidential.
Default `false`.

gcpWatermark.description:
Output only. Google-side scoring or eligibility watermark
for the opportunity. Provided as a numeric value; check
with your Google partner contact for current scoring
semantics.

dealNumber.description: Output only. System-generated unique deal identifier.

quantity.description: Optional. Number of seats or licenses. Default `1`.

publicSector.description:
Optional. Whether the customer is a public sector organization
that requires competing offers from multiple vendors.

campaignCode.description:
Optional. Active campaign name (issued by Google) for the
selected region and product. Campaign names are not
published in this API; check with your Google partner
contact for the valid values for your region and product
mix.

msspDeal.description:
Optional. Flag to highlight if the partner will also act as
MSSP (Managed Security Service Provider).

legalLanguageAccepted.description:
Required. Must be `true` for the opportunity to be created.
Cannot be edited after the opportunity is accepted.

publicTenderAttestation.description:
Required for public-sector opportunities (`publicSector:
true`); optional otherwise. Set to `true` to attest that
the opportunity meets public-tender requirements.

CustomerInfo.description: Customer information provided during opportunity creation.

CustomerDetails.description:
Customer details used to create a new customer or map to an
existing one.

organizationName.description: Required. Name of the customer organization.

employeeCount.description:
Required. Approximate total number of employees at the
customer organization.

PostalAddress.description:
A structured postal address compatible with Google's address
formatting model. For most regions, populate `regionCode`,
`addressLines`, `locality`, and `postalCode`; the remaining
fields cover country-specific cases (for example,
`administrativeArea` for state or province; `sortingCode` for
country-specific sorting codes such as France's CEDEX). See
https://support.google.com/business/answer/6397478 for
country-by-country guidance on which fields are required.

regionCode.description:
Required. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (also known as the
CLDR region code), for example `US`, `GB`, `DE`.

languageCode.description:
Optional. BCP-47 language tag for the address (for example,
`en-US`, `de-DE`). Used to disambiguate locale-specific
formatting.

sortingCode.description:
Optional. Country-specific sorting code (for example, CEDEX
in France). Most regions do not use this field.

administrativeArea.description:
Optional. Largest administrative subdivision below the
country level (for example, state, province, or region).

sublocality.description:
Optional. Smaller administrative subdivision below
`locality` (for example, neighborhood or district).

addressLines.description:
Optional. Street-address lines (street and number, suite or
unit). Order is preserved as-rendered.

recipients.description: Optional. Recipient name(s) at this address.

organization.description: Optional. Organization name at this address.

e164Number.description:
Phone number in ITU E.164 format, starting with `+`. For
example `+15552220123`.

PhoneNumberShortCode.description: A short code — region-restricted phone number.

regionCode.description:
Required. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (also known as the
CLDR region code).

IsvSolutionConnectInfo.description:
Information for an opportunity that goes through Google's ISV
Solution Connect program.

isvSolutionConnectDeal.description:
`true` if the deal is part of Google's ISV Solution
Connect program. Defaults to `false`.

customerContactRequested.description:
`true` when the customer has requested follow-up contact
from the ISV. Must be `true` for an ISV Solution Connect
opportunity to be accepted.

notes.description:
Optional. Only available for ISV opportunities. ISV and Google
use this to keep each other up to date on selling activity.

nextStep.description:
Optional. Only available for ISV opportunities. Summarizes the
next step and who takes it.

PartnerInfo.description: Partner information populated after the opportunity is accepted.

incentiveEligibility.description: Output only. Whether the partner is eligible for incentives.

extensionsCount.description: Output only. Number of extensions for rebate.

gcpProjectNumbers.description: Optional. Google Cloud project numbers. Numeric values only.

submitTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the opportunity was last submitted.

approveTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the opportunity was approved.

closeDatePushCount.description: Output only. Number of times close date is pushed/changed.

prmSiteDetails.description:
Output only. Reference to the opportunity in Google's
Partner Relationship Management (PRM) portal.

WinLossInfo.description:
Win / loss details. Populated after the opportunity is closed.
Output only.

lostReason.description: Output only. Free-form reason the opportunity was lost.

lostMainReason.description: Output only. Top-line categorization of the loss.

lostRejectedReasonDetails.description:
Output only. Additional detail provided when the opportunity
was rejected.

winMainReason.description: Output only. Top-line categorization of the win.

wonReason.description: Output only. Free-form reason the opportunity was won.

winLossProducts.description: Output only. Products attached to the win/loss outcome.

winLossAdditionalContext.description: Output only. Additional free-form context on the outcome.

displayName.description: Output only. Display name of the line item.

quantity.description: Output only. Number of units on the line item.

metric.description:
Output only. Unit of measure for `quantity` (for example,
`seats`, `licenses`, `gigabytes`).

description.description: Output only. Free-form description of the line item.

name.description: Output only. Display name of the team member.

email.description: Output only. Email address of the team member.

givenName.description: Output only. Given (first) name of the contact.

familyName.description: Output only. Family (last) name of the contact.

title.description: Output only. Job title at the customer organization.

primary.description:
Output only. True when this contact is marked as the
primary contact for the customer.

comments.description:
Output only. Free-form comments associated with the
extension request.

Money.description:
An amount of money with its currency type. The whole `Money`
object is replaced atomically when included on update — there is
no per-field merge of `currencyCode`, `units`, or `nanos`.

units.description:
Whole units of the amount, encoded as a string. For example,
`1500000` with `currencyCode: USD` and `nanos: 0` is
$1,500,000.00 USD.

nanos.description:
Sub-unit (nano) part of the amount. One unit equals 10^9
nanos; for example, `nanos: 750000000` represents 0.75 of
one unit. Must have the same sign as `units`.

Date.description:
A calendar date. Any field may be zero to represent a partial
date (for example, `year: 2026, month: 0, day: 0` for "sometime
in 2026"). The whole `Date` object is replaced atomically when
included on update — there is no per-field merge.

year.description: Year (1–9999), or 0 to specify a date without a year.

month.description: Month (1–12), or 0 to specify a year without a month and day.

day.description:
Day (1–31, valid for year+month), or 0 to specify year, or
year + month.

State.description:
Lifecycle state of the opportunity:

- `STATE_UNSPECIFIED` — placeholder default; should not be
  sent on requests.
- `DRAFT` — saved but not yet submitted to Google. Settable
  by integrators.
- `SUBMITTED` — submitted to Google for review. Settable by
  integrators (requires `cosell:StartEngagement`).
- `ACCEPTED` — Google has accepted the opportunity. Set by
  Google.
- `NOT_ACCEPTED` — Google has declined the opportunity. Set
  by Google.

Defaults to `DRAFT` when omitted on create.

Stage.description:
Sales stage of the opportunity. The `STAGE_UNSPECIFIED`,
`MIGRATION_IMPL`, `CLOSED_LOST`, and `CLOSED_ADMIN` values
are set only by the API on the integrator's behalf based on
other fields (for example, `partnerInfo.partnerReadyToClose`);
they cannot be set directly. The remaining values
(`QUALIFY`, `REFINE`, `TECH_EVAL_SOL_DEV`,
`PROPOSAL_NEGOTIATION`) can be set on update only after the
opportunity is `ACCEPTED`.

- `QUALIFY` — initial qualification.
- `REFINE` — qualification refined; deal scope being shaped.
- `TECH_EVAL_SOL_DEV` — technical evaluation / solution
  development.
- `PROPOSAL_NEGOTIATION` — proposal and negotiation.
- `MIGRATION_IMPL` — migration / implementation; corresponds
  to closed-won.
- `CLOSED_LOST` — opportunity closed as lost.
- `CLOSED_ADMIN` — administratively closed.

Source.description:
Indicates the origin of the opportunity:

- `SOURCE_UNKNOWN` — origin not recorded; should not be
  observed on supported responses.
- `GOOGLE` — sourced by a Google sales user.
- `GOOGLE_BDR` — sourced by a Google Business Development
  Representative.
- `GOOGLE_PROGRAMMATIC` — generated by a Google automated
  system.
- `PARTNER` — sourced by the partner (the integrator). The
  API forces this value on opportunities created via this
  spec.

OpportunityType.description:
Indicates if the opportunity is a regular / ISV / 2-tier deal. If
not specified, treated as `REGULAR`. Cannot be edited after the
opportunity is accepted.

OperationType.description:
Transaction type for the opportunity:

- `OPERATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` — placeholder default; should
  not be sent on create.
- `NEW` — net-new transaction with a new customer.
- `RENEWAL` — renewal of an existing subscription.
- `ADD_ON` — additional purchase on an existing customer.
- `EXPANSION` — expansion of an existing subscription
  (for example, more seats).

ProductFamily.description: Product family that the opportunity belongs to.

ProductCategory.description: Product category that the opportunity belongs to.

Region.description:
Geographical region where the end customer is located. The partner
needs sell authorization in this region to qualify for deal
registration incentives.

Budget.description:
Budget qualification. Required for regular and 2-tier
opportunities; optional for ISV opportunities.

SupportLevel.description: Support level for an ISV opportunity.

ContractVehicle.description: Contract vehicle for an ISV opportunity.

DeliveryModel.description: Delivery model for an ISV opportunity.

IncentiveType.description:
Output only. Incentive program the opportunity is eligible for:

- `INCENTIVE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` — eligibility not yet
  determined.
- `DEAL_REGISTRATION` — partner registers the deal up front
  and the registration drives the incentive.
- `DEAL_REFERRAL` — partner referred the deal but does not
  register it; incentive applies on a referral basis.

PartnerViewType.description:
Indicates what view the partner has access to. Non-sourcing
service partners have limited view; no updates are allowed on the
opportunity in `LIMITED` view. Output only.

PartnerReadyToClose.description:
Partner ready-to-close indicator. Can be edited after the
opportunity is accepted. Setting to `MIGRATION_IMPL` corresponds
to Closed/Won; setting to `CLOSED_LOST` corresponds to Closed/Lost.

AccessLevel.description: Access level for an opportunity team member.

Role.description:
Role of a customer contact. Most values are role categories that
apply to any opportunity; `CHRONICLE_SIEM_CONTACT` and
`CHRONICLE_SOAR_CONTACT` are specific to engagements involving
Google Chronicle (Google's SIEM and SOAR security products).

ExtensionRejectionReason.description: Rebate extension rejection reason. Output only.

TackleOperationIdCreate.description:
Tackle-side operation identifier accepted on the
`tackle-operation-id` header by `POST /api/opportunities`.
Only these two values are accepted; any other value
(including the broader update-side operations) is rejected
with a `400 Bad Request`.

TackleOperationIdUpdate.description:
Tackle-side operation identifier accepted on the
`tackle-operation-id` header by `POST /api/opportunities/{id}`.
The create-side values (`createOpportunity`,
`createDraftOpportunity`) are explicitly rejected with a
`400 Bad Request` — creates must be sent to
`POST /api/opportunities` instead. Test-environment-only operations
(`acceptOpportunity`, `rejectOpportunity`,
`closeByAdminOpportunity`, `confirmCloseWonOpportunity`,
`confirmCloseLostOpportunity`) are accepted only when the
calling vendor is configured for use in a test environment;
production vendors receive a `400 Bad Request` if they send
these values. The remaining operations apply to every vendor.

HistoryOperationId.description:
Operation identifier stored on history events returned by
`GET /api/opportunities/{id}/events`. Treated as a free-form
string on the wire: the documented values below cover the
common cases, but additional operation strings may appear as
new history sources are added. Clients should fall back to
a default branch when displaying an unknown value.

Common values include every operation accepted on the
`tackle-operation-id` header by the create and update
endpoints (see `TackleOperationIdCreate` and
`TackleOperationIdUpdate`) plus two service-emitted
operations:

- `internalUpdateEvent` — a Tackle metadata field on the
  opportunity changed (for example, the attribute-syncing
  subscription).
- `cloudUpdateEvent` — the opportunity's cloud payload
  (`cloudRaw`) was refreshed because Google Cloud Channel
  sent a new snapshot.

These two service-emitted values are never accepted as
`tackle-operation-id` headers; they appear only on history
events.
